quote:
When a storm roars across the world, the wise do not chase it, but stand firm in the root of their own inner garden.

The ground that trembles beneath great armor will swallow a clashing thunder if the heart does not learn to listen to the quiet before the clash.

In the great dance of nations, those who hold the rhythm still find their steps unbroken even when the music shifts.

A river forged in fire does not drown in heat; it learns to carve new paths among the rocks it once feared.

Power that flickers like a candle in a breeze is only as bright as the observer who keeps its flame steady.

The cloud that gathers the greatest water may bring both flood and fire, yet the wise know to hold dough in the palm of patience.

When the great wheel of expectation turns, the seeker who sits on the path watches the ridges, knowing the road will smooth itself.
quote_preview: When a storm roars across the world, the wise do not chase it, but stand firm in the root of their own inner garden.
